questions.title: Most Major Pro Sports Teams (NBA + NFL + MLB + NHL)
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by combined number of franchises across the four major pro leagues (NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL).
questions.disclaimer: Counts include only US-based franchises. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Official league franchise directories (NBA.com, NFL.com, MLB.com, NHL.com)

questions.title: Most Combined Major Pro Sports Championships (NBA + NFL + MLB + NHL)
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by total championships won by teams based in that state across NBA, NFL, MLB, and NHL (all-time).

source.name: Official league title records (NBA Finals, Super Bowl/NFL Championship, World Series, Stanley Cup)

questions.title: Most NCAA D1 Football National Championships
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by all-time NCAA Division I FBS football national championships won by teams headquartered in that state (recognized major-selector titles).
questions.disclaimer: Counts follow the widely recognized AP/Coaches/BCS/CFP claim lists. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: Wikipedia — College football national championships in NCAA Division I FBS

questions.title: Most Top 50 National Universities (US News)
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by number of universities in the US News Top 50 National Universities.
questions.disclaimer: Includes ties at #50. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US News & World Report - Best National Universities Rankings

questions.title: Most US Presidents Born in State
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by number of US Presidents born there (through the 47th presidency).
questions.disclaimer: Counts each US president by the state where they were born (through the 47th presidency). Only one state is credited per president. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).

source.name: White House Historical Association / National Archives

questions.title: Highest Share of Adults with a Graduate/Professional Degree
questions.prompt: Rank the US states (and DC) by percent of adults 25+ holding a graduate or professional degree (ACS 2022).
questions.disclaimer: Share of adults 25+ holding a graduate or professional degree, per the American Community Survey (2022 ACS 1-year). Includes DC as a state-level jurisdiction.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey (Educational Attainment table B15003)

questions.title: Highest Share of Adults with High School Diploma or Higher
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by percent of adults 25+ who have completed at least a high school diploma (ACS 2022).
questions.disclaimer: Share of adults 25+ with at least a high school diploma. Rates are very compressed near the top (roughly 92-95%). Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey (Educational Attainment table S1501)

questions.title: Most Museums (IMLS)
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by total number of museums recorded in the Institute of Museum and Library Services Museum Data File.
questions.disclaimer: IMLS counts include art museums, historical societies, historic sites, arboreta, zoos, aquariums, science and children's museums. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: IMLS Museum Data File
source.asOf: IMLS MDF v3 (2018 release; latest comprehensive)

questions.title: Most Public Library Systems (IMLS)
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by number of public library administrative entities (systems) reported to IMLS.
questions.disclaimer: Counts library administrative entities (systems), not branch locations. Includes Washington DC.

questions.title: Most Nobel Laureates by State of Birth (US-born winners)
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by number of Nobel laureates who were born there (all Nobel categories, all-time).
questions.disclaimer: Counts US-born laureates only (not naturalized or foreign-born winners affiliated with US institutions). Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Nobel Foundation - Nobel Prizes biographical data

questions.title: Highest Median Age
questions.prompt: Which US states have the highest median age?
questions.disclaimer: DC's median age skews younger due to its large young-adult professional population; DC is not among the leaders here.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates (Table B01002)

questions.title: Highest Foreign-Born Population Share
questions.prompt: Which US states have the highest share of foreign-born residents?
questions.disclaimer: Percentage of total population born outside the United States (includes naturalized citizens and non-citizens). Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates (Table B05002)

questions.title: Highest Homeownership Rate
questions.prompt: Which US states have the highest homeownership rate?
questions.disclaimer: Owner-occupied housing units as a share of all occupied housing units. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates (Table B25003)

questions.title: Highest Poverty Rate
questions.prompt: Which US states have the highest poverty rate?
questions.disclaimer: Share of the population with income below the official federal poverty threshold in the past 12 months. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates (Table S1701)

questions.title: Highest Bachelor's Degree Attainment
questions.prompt: Which US states have the highest share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher?
questions.disclaimer: Population age 25 and over holding at least a bachelor's degree. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates (Table S1501)

questions.title: Largest Hispanic or Latino Population Share
questions.prompt: Which US states have the largest Hispanic or Latino population share?
questions.disclaimer: Hispanic or Latino origin can be of any race per Census methodology. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates (Table B03003)
